analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of docs/reference/configuration.md (lines 1 onward and 219 onward), and the file is only modified. The supplied text contains no patch hunks, so I cannot tell which lines the PR changed. Only the top-of-file 'Last updated: 2026-10-05' stamp is visibly dated, and it may be the edit. I reviewed the visible content against the threat model and found nothing to flag.

The content is a documentation reference, with no executable code. It states that App Attest serving and MDM-removal opt-ins are disabled by default (TB-011, T-052..T-058). It says shadow evidence grants no trust and that durable build qualification overrides env bootstrap hashes (T-054). The cache-routing and SSD prefix-cache settings (T-041) and the Stripe, admin and MDM settings are documented consistently with the canonical model. The documented 30-minute SSD TTL, the 20 GiB reserve, and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch match T-041, and the TTFT and queue knobs are not security-relevant.

Coverage limit: the diff itself was not provided, and only the first part of the document appears to be included (the sidecar table is truncated). Later sections, and any change that weakens a documented default, may be missing from this review. A reviewer with the actual patch should check three things. First, whether any default for serving authorization, MDM removal, the min-trust floor (EIGENINFERENCE_MIN_TRUST), state export, or the plaintext-export allowance was changed. Second, whether the doc is now inconsistent with the code. Third, whether a documented default that differs from the compiled one could mislead operators.
